findings.title: Provisioning can restart the tick cluster without rechecking its lock
findings.description: The cutover checks for tick advisory locks earlier, then calls `provision_tick_cluster.sh`. That script’s settings path can restart the cluster when settings require it (`scripts/provision_tick_cluster.sh:204-210`), without checking those locks. A tick job can acquire a lock between the cutover’s initial check and this restart, so the later lock check in `step_restart` cannot prevent an interruption that has already happened. Recheck immediately before every restart, including the one reached through provisioning.

findings.title: Health verification can accept a stale successful log entry
findings.description: `run_health` ignores the `CompletedProcess` returned by `shell()` and reads the last line already present in the health log. If the command fails before appending a new line, the cutover can parse an older `FLAGS archive=0 stale=0` entry and pass verification. Check the command’s return code and ensure the log entry was produced by this invocation before accepting its flags.

findings.title: A rerun after cron installation fails the production comparison
findings.description: `production_changes` compares the old production lines unchanged against new lines after stripping the 227 arguments. On a rerun, `step_check` captures the already-updated cron file as `old_cron`, so the old lines still contain those arguments and the comparison reports them as unexpected changes. This prevents the documented fix-and-rerun recovery path after a failure later in the cutover. Normalize both sides or explicitly handle an already-rendered cron file, and test that rerunning after installation succeeds.
